title: TransDANN-Surv: When Domain-Adversarial Training (GRL/DANN) Fails in Cross-Population Cancer Survival Prediction
description: Large-scale mechanistic evidence that gradient-reversal domain-adversarial training (GRL/DANN) fails to improve cross-population cancer survival prediction: the distribution of cohort-level covariates (age, stage, event rate), of which missingness patterns are only the most visible surface, is the fundamental domain fingerprint. A domain classifier reaches 97-98% and cannot be suppressed by gradient reversal; controlled imputation (missingness to 0%) leaves it at 97.7%; and a leakage-free within-cohort imputation cannot fill fields that are structurally unobservable in a cohort. Input-level augmentation (mixup) is the only method surviving Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. This archive contains all analysis scripts, paper figures (Figures 1-8, S1-S5), and result tables (table1-19, Table S1-S7). Raw cohort data are not redistributed (TCGA, SEER, and cBioPortal license terms); they are reproducible via the documented download scripts.
